steps.title: Turn the printer off and on again
steps.detail: Switch it off, unplug it for 30 seconds, plug it back in and switch it on.
steps.why: Restarting clears most stuck print jobs.
steps.source_name: Microsoft: Fix printer connection and printing problems in Windows

steps.title: Check paper, ink and the connection
steps.detail: Check that it has paper and ink and shows no error. Check the cable, or that it is on the same Wi-Fi as the computer.
steps.why: A printer on another network or with an error light cannot print.
steps.source_name: Microsoft: Fix printer connection and printing problems in Windows

steps.title: Remove the printer and add it again
steps.detail: In Windows Settings, open Printers, remove this printer, then add it again.
steps.why: This fixes a broken printer setup on the computer.
steps.source_name: Microsoft: Fix printer connection and printing problems in Windows

steps.title: Ask your IT contact to clear the print queue
steps.detail: If jobs stay stuck, the print spooler may need to be cleared and restarted. Your IT contact can do it in a few minutes.
steps.why: A stuck job can block every print after it.
steps.source_name: Microsoft: Fix printer connection and printing problems in Windows

steps.title: Still stuck? Call your IT contact
steps.detail: Tell them what you tried and what you see on screen. A photo of the screen helps.
steps.why: They can check settings and equipment you cannot reach.
